final_answer:
Let  
\[
N=3^r,\qquad m=\frac n2=2q^2,\qquad a=\frac{q(2q-1)}{3^r}\in \mathbb Z
\]
(the integrality of \(a\) is exactly \(2q\equiv1\pmod{3^r}\)).

**1. The lifts of \(\pi\).**  
By the given cube-independence hypothesis, \(L/M\) is an elementary abelian \(3\)-extension, and every \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbf Q(\omega))\) with \(\pi_\sigma=\pi\) is uniquely determined by
\[
\sigma(\rho_j)=\omega^{b_j}\rho_j,\qquad
\sigma(\alpha_i^{(j)})=\omega^{c_i^{(j)}}\alpha_{\pi(i)}^{(j)},
\]
with \(b_j,c_i^{(j)}\in\mathbf F_3\), subject to
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n c_i^{(j)}=0\qquad(1\le j\le r).
\]
The condition \(\sigma(\rho_j)\ne \rho_j\) is exactly \(b_j\in\{1,2\}\), so there are \(2^r\) choices for \(b=(b_1,\dots,b_r)\).

Write the transpositions of \(\pi\) as \(P_1,\dots,P_m\), with \(P_t=\{x_t,y_t\}\).  
For each \(t,j\), define
\[
E_t^{(j)}=c_{x_t}^{(j)}+c_{y_t}^{(j)}\in\mathbf F_3,
\qquad
E_t=(E_t^{(1)},\dots,E_t^{(r)})\in \mathbf F_3^r.
\]
Since \(\sum_i c_i^{(j)}=0\), we have
\[
\sum_{t=1}^m E_t=0\in \mathbf F_3^r.
\]

**2. When do all \(\Omega_k\) have the same cycle type?**  
An element of \(\Omega_k\) is indexed by \((i,\ell,u)\) with \(i\ne \ell\), \(u\in\mathbf F_3^r\), and \(\sigma\) acts by
\[
(i,\ell,u)\mapsto \bigl(\pi(i),\pi(\ell),\,u+k\odot b+c_i-c_\ell\bigr),
\]
where \(\odot\) is coordinatewise multiplication.

Applying \(\sigma\) twice gives
\[
(i,\ell,u)\mapsto
\bigl(i,\ell,\,u+2(k\odot b)+E_{p(i)}-E_{p(\ell)}\bigr),
\]
where \(p(i)\in\{1,\dots,m\}\) is the transposition-pair containing \(i\). Since \(2=-1\) in \(\mathbf F_3\), the square is the identity on the \(u\)-coordinate exactly when
\[
E_{p(i)}-E_{p(\ell)}=k\odot b.
\]
Hence on each \(\pi\)-orbit of ordered pairs \((i,\ell)\), the induced cycle length is:

- \(2\), if \(E_{p(i)}-E_{p(\ell)}=k\odot b\);
- \(6\), otherwise.

So the cycle type on \(\Omega_k\) depends only on the number of ordered-pair orbits with difference \(k\odot b\). Since every \(b_j\neq0\), the map \(k\mapsto k\odot b\) is a bijection of \(\mathbf F_3^r\). Thus the cycle type is the same for all \(k\) iff those counts are constant as \(v\) runs over \(\mathbf F_3^r\).

Let \(\nu_x=\#\{t:E_t=x\}\) for \(x\in \mathbf F_3^r\). A standard count gives:
\[
\#\{\text{zero-translation pair-orbits for }v\}=
\begin{cases}
m+2\sum_x \nu_x(\nu_x-1),&v=0,\\[1mm]
2\sum_x \nu_x\nu_{x-v},&v\ne0.
\end{cases}
\]
Therefore the cycle types are all equal iff
\[
\sum_x \nu_x\nu_{x-v}
=
\begin{cases}
\mu+q^2,&v=0,\\
\mu,&v\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
for some \(\mu\).

Now set \(f(x)=\nu_x-a\). Since \(\sum_x \nu_x=m=aN+q\), we get \(\sum_x f(x)=q\), and the above becomes
\[
\sum_x f(x)f(x-v)=q^2\,\delta_{v,0}.
\]
Take Fourier transforms on \(G=\mathbf F_3^r\). For every character \(\chi\) of \(G\),
\[
|\widehat f(\chi)|^2=q^2.
\]
Also \(\widehat f(\chi)\in \mathbf Z[\omega]\). Because \(q\equiv2\pmod3\), any \(z\in\mathbf Z[\omega]\) with \(|z|=q\) is divisible by \(q\) in \(\mathbf Z[\omega]\): indeed if \(z=u+v\omega\) and \(q\nmid v\), then \((u/v)^2-(u/v)+1\equiv0\pmod q\), which would give an element of order \(3\) in \(\mathbf F_q^\times\), impossible since \(3\nmid(q-1)\). So \(q\mid \widehat f(\chi)\) for every \(\chi\).

The Fourier matrix on \(G\) is invertible modulo \(q\) because \(|G|=3^r\) is prime to \(q\). Hence \(q\mid f(x)\) for every \(x\). Write \(f(x)=q h(x)\) with \(h(x)\in\mathbf Z\). Then
\[
\sum_x h(x)=1,\qquad \sum_x h(x)^2=1,
\]
so exactly one \(h(x)\) equals \(1\) and all others are \(0\). Thus
\[
f=q\,\delta_t
\]
for some \(t\in G\). Equivalently,
\[
\nu_t=a+q,\qquad \nu_x=a\ \ (x\ne t).
\]

Finally, \(\sum_t E_t=0\) forces \(t=0\), because
\[
\sum_{x\in G} x\,\nu_x
= q t + a\sum_{x\in G}x
= q t,
\]
and multiplication by \(q\) is invertible on \(G\). Therefore the necessary and sufficient multiplicities are
\[
\nu_0=a+q,\qquad \nu_x=a\ \ (x\ne0).
\]

**3. Counting.**  
So the \(m\) transposition-pairs must be labeled by elements of \(\mathbf F_3^r\) with multiplicities
\[
0:\ a+q,\qquad x\ne0:\ a.
\]
The number of such labelings is
\[
\frac{m!}{(a+q)!\,(a!)^{N-1}}.
\]

For each fixed labeling \(E_1,\dots,E_m\), and for each pair \(P_t=\{x_t,y_t\}\) and each \(j\), the equation
\[
c_{x_t}^{(j)}+c_{y_t}^{(j)}=E_t^{(j)}
\]
has exactly \(3\) solutions in \(\mathbf F_3^2\). Hence the number of corresponding \(c_i^{(j)}\) is
\[
3^{mr}=3^{2rq^2}.
\]

Multiplying by the \(2^r\) choices of \(b_j\in\{1,2\}\), the required number of \(\sigma\) is
\[
2^r\cdot 3^{2rq^2}\cdot \frac{(2q^2)!}{(a+q)!\,(a!)^{3^r-1}},
\qquad a=\frac{q(2q-1)}{3^r}.
\]

Final answer:
\[
\boxed{
2^r\,3^{2rq^2}\,
\frac{(2q^2)!}{
\left(q+\frac{q(2q-1)}{3^r}\right)!\,
\left(\frac{q(2q-1)}{3^r}!\right)^{3^r-1}
}
}
\]
equivalently,
\[
\boxed{
2^r\,3^{2rq^2}\,
\frac{(2q^2)!}{
\left(\frac{q(2q-1)}{3^r}+q\right)!\,
\left(\frac{q(2q-1)}{3^r}!\right)^{3^r-1}
}.
}
\]
